name: coordinator
description: Start a task graph: dispatch one root TaskNode of a mapping domain. This is the only way a route begins, because root nodes are never auto-dispatched.
notes: Exactly one tool. Everything else the coordinator does is driven by Kafka events, and a read surface would duplicate the domain MCPs.

Root nodes are never dispatched by a formal_revision_published event. Publishing a route does not start it — this call starts it. That is deliberate: a graph that begins work the moment someone saves it cannot be reviewed before it spends money.
The node must exist in the latest formal snapshot and have no inbound edges. Both are re-checked server-side; a stale task_node_id or a node with an inbound edge is refused, not silently started.
Idempotent through the handoff dedupe key, so a double click does not start the same root twice.

There is no tool here to dispatch a non-root node: downstream nodes start when their upstream handoff lands. Reaching for this to unblock a stuck successor will not work and would bypass the dependency edges.

tools.name: dispatch_root_task
tools.description: Explicitly dispatch one root task node of a mapping domain. The node must exist in the latest formal snapshot and have no inbound edges; the call is idempotent through the handoff dedupe key.
allowed: starting a route the formal mapping already publishes
